equation_request.abstract:
We give a quantum algorithm for evaluating formulas over an extended gate set, including all twoand three-bit binary gates (e.g., NAND, 3-majority). The algorithm is optimal on read-once formulas for which each gate's inputs are balanced in a certain sense.

The main new tool is a correspondence between a classical linear-algebraic model of computation, "span programs," and weighted bipartite graphs. A span program's evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the associated graph. A quantum computer can therefore evaluate the span program by applying spectral estimation to the graph.

For example, the classical complexity of evaluating the balanced ternary majority formula is unknown, and the natural generalization of randomized alpha-beta pruning is known to be suboptimal. In contrast, our algorithm generalizes the optimal quantum AND-OR formula evaluation algorithm and is optimal for evaluating the balanced ternary majority formula.

specification.problem: Evaluate a Boolean formula over an extended gate set (e.g. NAND, 3-majority) by encoding each gate as a span program, mapping it to a weighted bipartite graph, and using spectral estimation to detect an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scope: one tiny instance, a single 3-majority gate (a depth-1 formula) as a span program, with its associated bipartite graph and the eigenvalue-zero phase-estimation test. Out of scope: the full recursive formula-evaluation algorithm, the balance conditions, optimality and complexity proofs, the specific weights and graph construction for general gates, and the ternary majority tree analysis.

equations.label: 3-majority gate
equations.description: Definition of the example gate function.
equations.justification: Standard definition of 3-majority, named in the abstract.

equations.label: Span program evaluation condition
equations.latex: f(x)=1 \iff t \in \mathrm{span}\{v_j : \text{literal } j \text{ is satisfied by } x\}
equations.description: Generic span program acceptance rule: accept iff the target lies in the span of the vectors of satisfied literals.
equations.justification: Standard span-program definition recalled from background; the abstract only says span programs are a linear-algebraic model of computation.
assumptions: Standard Karchmer-Wigderson-style definition; the paper's variant may differ

equations.label: Evaluation as eigenvalue-zero eigenvector
equations.description: The evaluation of the span program corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the associated graph (precise eigenvector structure not specified here).
equations.abstract_quote: A span program's evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the associated graph.
equations.justification: Inferred loosely from the quoted claim; the abstract does not specify which outcome corresponds to the zero eigenvector, nor the exact eigenvector requirement, so the direction of the equivalence is an assumption.
assumptions: Zero-eigenvector existence (suitably restricted to an input-dependent subspace) corresponds to one function value

equations.label: Spectral estimation test
equations.latex: \text{phase estimation of } e^{iA_G} \text{ to precision } \epsilon:\ |\lambda|<\epsilon \Rightarrow \text{declare eigenvalue }0
equations.description: Decide zero versus nonzero eigenvalue by estimating the spectrum of A_G, using a unitary such as exp(i A_G).
equations.abstract_quote: A quantum computer can therefore evaluate the span program by applying spectral estimation to the graph.
equations.justification: Spectral estimation is named; the use of e^{iA_G} and the threshold rule are standard phase-estimation choices, not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Access to a method to implement e^{iA_G} or a similar unitary
Threshold epsilon chosen below the gap of nonzero eigenvalues

registers.name: graph
registers.role: Vertex register on which A_G acts; basis states are graph vertices

specification.initial_state: Assumed: a fixed start state on a designated vertex of G (e.g. the root/output vertex) in the graph register, with phase register in |0>.

steps.description: Choose the span program for the gate and build the bipartite graph G(x) with input-dependent structure.
Prepare the start state on the graph register and apply phase estimation of a unitary derived from A_G.
Interpret a phase near zero as evidence for the zero-eigenvalue case that corresponds to the evaluation outcome.

specification.measurement: Measure the phase register; outcome near zero indicates overlap with the eigenvalue-zero eigenspace.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Threshold the measured phase against epsilon to output the Boolean value; repeat to amplify success probability (assumed).
assumptions: The 3-majority single gate is chosen as the smallest useful instance.
Standard span program definition is used, not necessarily the paper's.
Graph weights and eigenvector structure are unspecified and left abstract.
